name: Yield re-entry
description: What happens when a host Service calls back into the block the guest handed it.

scenarios.title: A Service can tell that the guest passed it a block
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that reports whether it was given a block
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a block
scenarios.then: the Service reports that it was

scenarios.title: And that it was not
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that reports whether it was given a block
scenarios.when: guest code calls it without a block
scenarios.then: the Service reports that it was not

scenarios.title: Yielding answers with what the block said
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields once
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a block returning a value
scenarios.then: the Service receives that value from the yield

scenarios.title: Yielding several times runs the block each time
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields several times
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a block
scenarios.then: the block runs once per yield

scenarios.title: A block may reach back out to another Service
given: a Sandbox with two bound Services, one of which yields
scenarios.when: guest code's block calls the other Service
scenarios.then: the nested call answers and the outer yield receives the block's value

scenarios.title: A Service given a block need not use it
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that never yields
scenarios.when: guest code calls it with a block
scenarios.then: the call answers and the block never runs

scenarios.title: Breaking out of a block unwinds the Service
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields
scenarios.when: guest code's block breaks with a value
scenarios.then: the call answers that value without the Service finishing

scenarios.title: Breaking out of a lambda leaves the Service running
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields to a lambda
scenarios.when: the lambda breaks with a value
scenarios.then: the yield receives that value and the Service continues

scenarios.title: A break value the wire cannot carry is refused
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields
scenarios.when: guest code's block breaks with a value having no wire representation
scenarios.then: the invocation fails rather than carrying it across

scenarios.title: Each nested frame carries its own block
given: a Sandbox with bound Services yielding into one another
scenarios.when: guest code drives two nested yields
scenarios.then: each frame yields to the block it was given

scenarios.title: A refused nested call leaves the outer block usable
given: a Sandbox with bound Services yielding into one another
scenarios.when: the inner call is refused and the outer block runs on
scenarios.then: the outer yield still answers

scenarios.title: A raise inside the block surfaces where the Service yielded
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields
scenarios.when: guest code's block raises
scenarios.then: the Service sees the failure at its yield

scenarios.title: An unrescued block raise stays the guest's own exception
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that yields
scenarios.when: guest code's block raises and nobody rescues it
scenarios.then: the guest can rescue it as the exception it raised

scenarios.title: A Service that rescues the block reports its own failure instead
given: a Sandbox with a bound Service that rescues what its yield raised
scenarios.when: guest code's block raises
scenarios.then: the guest sees the Service's failure rather than its own

scenarios.title: A rescued block failure leaves nothing behind
given: a Sandbox whose Service rescued a raise from the block it yielded to
scenarios.when: the invocation continues
scenarios.then: no trace of that failure reaches the next yield

scenarios.title: A held failure answers only for the block that raised it
given: a Sandbox whose Service holds a failure from one block
scenarios.when: another block is yielded to
scenarios.then: the held failure does not answer for it

scenarios.title: A rescued failure does not answer that block's later refusal
given: a Sandbox whose Service rescued one failure from a block
scenarios.when: the same block is refused later for another reason
scenarios.then: the later refusal is reported as its own

scenarios.title: A reference in the block's answer becomes its object
given: a yield whose block answered with a capability reference
scenarios.when: the Service receives the answer
scenarios.then: it holds the original host object

scenarios.title: An answer carrying no reference crosses unchanged
given: a yield whose block answered with an ordinary value
scenarios.when: the Service receives the answer
scenarios.then: it holds that value unchanged

scenarios.title: A break value is not restored on its way out
given: a yield whose block broke with a capability reference
scenarios.when: the break unwinds
scenarios.then: the reference passes through without being restored

scenarios.title: Both frontends yield and answer the same way
given: a scenario whose Service yields once to a guest block
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same value

scenarios.title: Both unwind a break and fall through a next the same way
given: a scenario exercising both block exits
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same values

scenarios.title: Both carry a nested dispatch through a block the same way
given: a scenario whose block dispatches to another Service
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they observe the same value

scenarios.title: Both refuse a block exit aimed past the boundary the same way
given: a scenario whose block tries to leave past the yield boundary
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they refuse it the same way

scenarios.title: Both surface an unrescued block raise the same way
given: a scenario whose block raises with nobody to rescue it
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they attribute it the same way

text: A yield turns one dispatch into a conversation: the guest calls out, the host
calls back, and either side may end it. The scenarios follow every way that
conversation can close — a value, a break, a fall-through, a raise — because
The block-failure scenarios are about what a failure leaves behind. A Service
that rescues one raise, holds it, and yields again must not answer the second
block with the first block's failure, and a failure already rescued must not
reappear as a later refusal. Both are witnessed because neither shows up in
A block's answer is restored on its way in and a break's value is not, which
is the one asymmetry here; the exits that raise belong to the error taxonomy
